subject.title: [Bug]: Multiple independent paths cause duplicate Telegram messages

question: When final-delivery state survives a restart after platform-send evidence exists but Telegram acceptance cannot be reconciled, should OpenClaw suppress replay by default or preserve at-least-once delivery?
rationale: The runtime cannot guarantee both no duplicates and no message loss for an ambiguous non-idempotent send; the permanent recovery contract requires maintainer intent before changing user-visible semantics.

options.title: Suppress ambiguous replay
options.body: Treat any platform-send evidence as terminal unknown/failed, avoid a second Telegram send, and surface diagnostics or recovery status instead.

options.title: Preserve at-least-once delivery
options.body: Continue replaying ambiguous pending finals after restart, accepting that some users may receive duplicate messages.

options.title: Require reconciliation ledger
options.body: Pause the residual recovery change until a durable receipt or delivery-intent ledger can reconcile acceptance without guessing.

recommendation.title: Suppress ambiguous replay
recommendation.body: Treat any platform-send evidence as terminal unknown/failed, avoid a second Telegram send, and surface diagnostics or recovery status instead.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent drain-side hardening established the closest existing contract for refusing replay after post-send evidence.
